subtype: Approach: tries the same action in different ways until something works [Action]
passage: Nursery note. Baljeet, two, sat on the mat with the shape box and pushed the round block at the square hole. It did not go. Baljeet turned it over and pushed again, then pressed harder with both hands and grunted. Then Baljeet tried the round hole, and the block dropped in with a clunk. Baljeet clapped and looked up at me. I only smiled. Preeti, sitting beside, tried the same block in the square hole and laughed.

qa.q: What sound did the block make?
qa.a: The block dropped in with a clunk.

qa.q: How did Baljeet seem to feel when the block dropped in?
qa.a: Baljeet seemed pleased and proud, clapping and looking up at the adult.

qa.q: What could the caregiver do next time Baljeet is stuck?
qa.a: The caregiver could let Baljeet keep trying and give a small hint only if Baljeet gets upset.

qa.q: How might Preeti have seen what Baljeet did?
qa.a: Preeti was probably curious, since Preeti tried the same block in the square hole and laughed.

grounding: Shows a toddler trying a round block in a square hole by turning it and pressing harder, then moving to the round hole where it drops in.

passage:
On the veranda of Nani's house, Karthik sat with the wooden shape box. He picked up the round red block and pushed it at the square hole. It stuck. He turned it and pushed harder. Stuck.
He banged it once and looked at cousin Eshaan.
Eshaan just watched.
Karthik moved his hand. Round block, round hole. Plop! It dropped inside.
He peered in, then grabbed the next block.

qa.q: What colour was the round block?
How might Karthik have felt when the block kept sticking?
qa.a: He was probably frustrated, which is why he banged it once and looked at Eshaan.

qa.q: What could Eshaan do if Karthik gets very upset next time?
qa.a: Eshaan could point gently at the right hole or show one block, but still let Karthik push it in himself.

qa.q: How might Eshaan see Karthik's plop moment?
qa.a: Eshaan may feel pleased and amused, seeing Karthik work it out without any help.

grounding: It shows a toddler turning and pushing a round block at the wrong hole, then trying another hole and learning from the success.

subtype: Approach: tries the same action in different ways until something works [Action]
passage:
In the park in Seville, Diego sat on the blanket with a plastic shape bucket. Aiko, the little girl from the next blanket, crawled closer.
Diego pressed the yellow circle into the square slot. Push. Push. He turned it. He pressed with both hands. Nothing.
He moved it to the next slot. Nothing. Next slot. Drop!
He squealed and clapped. Then he picked up the yellow circle again and dropped it into the round slot, straight away.

qa.a: Diego sat on the blanket in the park in Seville.

qa.q: How did Diego feel when the circle dropped in?
qa.a: He felt happy and excited, which is why he squealed and clapped. 🙂

qa.q: What could an adult nearby do to help Diego learn without taking over?
qa.a: They could sit near him and cheer each try, letting him keep turning and testing the block himself.

qa.q: How might Aiko see Diego's squeal and clap?
qa.a: Aiko may be curious and excited too, and may want to try dropping a shape in herself.

grounding: It shows a toddler turning and pressing a circle at the wrong slots, then trying another slot and learning from the success without words.
